clue.text: Man working to safeguard prominent lady?

definitions.text: Man working to safeguard prominent lady?

indicators.note: to safeguard someone is to keep them protected on all sides, so the other letters close around the lady

parts.note: a chap is a man
a machine that is on is working
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the most prominent lady of all

explanation.surface: A question about a man whose job is to protect a famous woman, perhaps a bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's standard Queen. The whole clue doubles as definition: a chaperon guards a lady's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort who keeps watch over a young or important woman in company is exactly this kind of protector.

clue.text: Maybe a BA with first in English, top mark

parts.note: a holder of a BA degree is, for example, a grad

indicators.note: the first letter of the word English is what this phrase asks for

explanation.surface: A graduate in English who got a first and so earned the highest mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The best grade awarded in exams is an A, so the top result is spoken of this way.

clue.text: Rarely seen wearing casual clothes at university and work

parts.note: someone dressed in shorts is wearing casual clothes
UP is the British idiom for being in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'
to ply a trade is to work at it

explanation.surface: Someone who seldom appears in shorts at college or at their job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is hard to find, so it is seldom met with; the idiom names that scarcity.

clue.text: Band's second drug-induced experience, taking ecstasy

parts.note: a trip is a hallucinatory episode on drugs
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A rock band's second hallucinatory episode, brought on by ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow strip of colour across a surface is a band, as on a flag.

clue.text: Fellow having soldiers surrounded in old battle site

indicators.note: the fellow has the soldiers held within him
the soldiers are surrounded, enclosed by the letters for the fellow

parts.note: BOD is British slang for a person or fellow
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A man whose troops were encircled at a historic battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: BORODINO is the 1812 battle near Moscow between Napoleon and the Russians.
explanation.definitionFit: The village west of Moscow is famous as the place of a bloody Napoleonic engagement.

clue.text: Clever pupil shows this book just when meeting the head

parts.note: just means fair or right
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: A smart schoolchild reveals a book exactly when meeting the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' suggests a schoolchild, but the definition also plays on the eye's pupil, which shows light.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in a child is called being bright, so a clever student displays that quality.

clue.text: Noise made by cat chasing small duck

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the cat's noise comes after the small letter

parts.note: a mew is a cat's cry

explanation.surface: A cat mewing as it goes after a little duck.
explanation.definitionFit: This small diving bird with white plumage is a species of sawbill duck.

clue.text: Quiet ayatollah gutted former Middle Eastern ruler

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet

indicators.note: a gutted thing has had its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters of ayatollah

explanation.surface: A hushed Iranian cleric, emptied out, recalls the king of old.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ayatollah replaced the monarch of Iran in 1979, so the surface fits its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the kings of Persia, later Iran, before the 1979 revolution.

clue.text: Crises one's resolved in economically-challenging periods

indicators.note: a crisis resolved is sorted out, so these letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Emergencies being sorted out during economic hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Spells of shrinking economic activity, with falling output, are the hard times named.

clue.text: Performing in cabaret without energy, one has the hump repeatedly

indicators.note: performing means putting on a show, so the letters are reworked
without tells us one letter is left out of the mix

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone sulking time and again while appearing in cabaret, too tired to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Performing' rearranges IN CABARET once 'without' has dropped its E. 'Has the hump' means sulking, but here it is literal: two humps.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-humped camel of Central Asia carries a hump more than once.

clue.text: Blokeish male into culture

parts.note: HE is the male pronoun
someone arty is keen on the arts

explanation.surface: A laddish man who is nonetheless keen on the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and boisterously sporty in a jolly, back-slapping way describes a bluff, matey type.

clue.text: State school in a rut, transformed by head of academy

indicators.note: something transformed has been changed in form, so the letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A state school stuck in a rut, turned around by an academy's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges SCHOOL IN A RUT, and the A from academy finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states, on the Atlantic coast between Georgia and its northern twin.

clue.text: Legion turned back helpless dairymaid

indicators.note: turned back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
help-less means without help, and help is aid, so those three letters go

explanation.surface: A milkmaid turned away, with no one to help her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helpless' splits as help-less: remove AID (help) from DAIRYMAID to leave DAIRYM, which 'turned back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in 'their faults are legion', it means countless, a huge number.

clue.text: They learn there's lots of water in river

indicators.note: the rain is placed in the river

parts.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England
rain is a great deal of water falling

explanation.surface: Pupils discover there's a heavy downpour falling into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: People under instruction in a job or skill are the ones doing the learning.

clue.text: Jack is hard on confounded Tories

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so this letter sits atop the rest

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Jack is tough on the baffled Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a man's name; here it is a lifting device.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a device for raising heavy loads, so it is a lifter.

clue.text: Celebrate with trainer, say, briefly recruited by former Wimbledon winner?

indicators.note: recruited by means taken into, so these letters go inside the former

parts.note: past means former
to sing is to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, dropping the last letter

parts.note: a trainer is an example of a shoe

explanation.surface: A former Wimbledon champion takes on a coach to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wimbledon winner' suggests a champion, but a winner is also a point-winning stroke in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke that beats an opponent at the net by going past them is a classic point-winner.

clue.text: Right smooth wine from this area?

parts.note: to hone is to smooth or sharpen

explanation.surface: A wine that is just right and smooth, and you wonder where it comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The river valley in south-east France gives its name to Côtes du Rhône wines grown there.

clue.text: Somebody incompetent

definitions.meaning: an important person, a somebody, as a noun
read as two words, it means lacking ability

explanation.surface: Somebody who is incompetent.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous figure is a somebody, while split in two the word says lacking the capacity.

clue.text: A number of pints one's brought in for people getting tanked?

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so these letters go within the pints

parts.note: a quart is two pints
one's means one is, giving I (one) plus S

explanation.surface: Drinkers who have sunk several pints and got drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanked' suggests drunk, fitting the pints; here it means keeping fish in tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobbyists who keep fish in aquariums spend their time with water tanks.

clue.text: Style of pop music a hit

definitions.meaning: a genre of spoken rhythmic lyrics over a beat

explanation.surface: A kind of pop music that's a chart success.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-hop's chanted lyrics name the genre, while a smart knock on the knuckles is a blow.

clue.text: Poet describes the old lady of society

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw around it, so the poet goes around these letters

parts.note: John Donne was an English poet
ye is an old form of 'the', as in 'Ye Olde Tea Shoppe'

explanation.surface: A poet writes about the old woman of high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior and most respected woman in a group or field is its grande dame.

clue.text: Where to arrive from foreign terminus, crossing Iran's borders

parts.note: de is French and Spanish for from

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the borders of Iran sit within the station

parts.note: a terminus is a railway station at the end of the line

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A traveller's route from a foreign terminal across Iran's frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The end point of a journey is the place you are heading for and reach.

clue.text: Polluted lake is kept free of last of oil

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

indicators.note: free of means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: kept means held

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, here the one that ends the word oil

explanation.surface: A lake is polluted, yet kept clear of the final traces of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sullied or stained, especially a reputation, has been dirtied or spoilt.

clue.text: Gossip picked up in this place, for example

indicators.note: picked up means caught by ear, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: here means in this place
say means for example

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle overheard around here, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Unverified information passed on by word of mouth is rumour, the stuff of tittle-tattle.

clue.text: Maybe phone business over new form of diplomacy

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Perhaps call the firm about a new style of diplomacy.
explanation.definitionFit: To get in touch with someone, by phone for instance, is to reach them.

clue.text: One's cracked shell

definitions.meaning: a person who is crazy, cracked in the head
read as two words, the hard outer casing of a nut

explanation.surface: Someone whose outer casing is broken.
explanation.definitionFit: A mad person is said to be cracked, and a nut's outer husk is its casing.

clue.text: Houses back-to-back at top of a row

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the top of means placed above, so these letters come first

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house; two of them back to back gives HO and its mirror image

explanation.surface: Back-to-back houses at the end of a terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-to-back houses are a British style of terraced housing; here 'back-to-back' sets one HO facing the other, HO then OH.
explanation.definitionFit: A row here rhymes with cow: a noisy commotion or fuss.

clue.text: One has no time for academic environment

indicators.note: has no means lacks, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a unit is one

explanation.surface: Someone with no spare time for the academic world.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for university, the college setting where academics study and work.
